primitives.does: Record CLOSURE_REQUESTED, and determine who requested it, whether they hold the authority to, the account's current state, its open blockers and its dependent relationships

primitives.asks: Does the requester hold authority to close this account?

branches.label: Authorised
branches.test: they own the account or hold the role that may close it

branches.label: Not authorised
branches.test: the request comes from someone who cannot make it

primitives.brief: Tell the requester that no closure took place and why this request cannot perform it, without disclosing account state they are not entitled to. A closure request that disappears leaves the requester believing an account is closed when it is not

primitives.purpose: Name the state that prevents closure, without inventing a route around it.
primitives.brief: Name the state that prevents closure, without inventing a route around it. Where nothing the requester can do would change it, saying so is the answer - an unresolvable block reported as silence reads as a request still being processed

primitives.purpose: Confirm the account relationship is closed and state plainly what closure is not - it is not subscription cancellation and it is not data deletion, both of which have their own lifecycles and their own evidence.
primitives.brief: Confirm the account relationship is closed and state plainly what closure is not - it is not subscription cancellation and it is not data deletion, both of which have their own lifecycles and their own evidence. Sent only after closure is verified, never on the request

branches.label: Blocked, recoverable
branches.test: an active financial obligation, an open transaction, a required return, a security review, a dependent entity or an administrative process stands in the way and can be resolved

branches.label: Blocked, not recoverable
branches.test: something prevents closure that the account holder cannot resolve

primitives.brief: Surface the exact blocker. Telling someone they cannot close their account without saying why produces a support case rather than a closure, and it reads as an obstacle rather than a requirement

mustNotClaim: a route around the blocker that does not exist

cancelOn.meaning: the blocker that prevented closure is resolved

primitives.reads: the the account and this closure request re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

primitives.asks: With that blocker resolved, is anything else in the way?

branches.label: Further blockers
branches.test: resolving one revealed or left others

primitives.state: one blocker cleared, others remain and are surfaced
primitives.reEntry: each remaining blocker is named and resolved on its own, and closure is requested again - stacking them into one message tells the account holder nothing they can act on

primitives.state: closure request lapsed with blockers outstanding
primitives.reEntry: a fresh request re-enters against whatever blockers still stand
the preventing condition changing re-opens this. The account stays open and the reason is on record rather than left as an unexplained refusal

primitives.does: Execute the account closure. This ends the account relationship and does nothing else - it cancels no subscription unless a contract explicitly couples them, and it deletes no data. The audit and history are untouched
Verify the account is no longer active for the operations closure prohibits

branches.label: Closed
branches.test: the account no longer permits prohibited operations

primitives.on: a closure that has taken effect on the account itself
carries: the closed account and the dependent relationships identified at request time
the explicit fact that no external or commercial dependency has been terminated by this

primitives.on: a closure that did not fully apply
